name: Ambedkarism
summary: Ambedkarism is the social and political thought of B. R. Ambedkar: abolition of caste by rejecting the shastras that sanction it, equality as the governing principle, constitutional parliamentary democracy with enforceable rights and group safeguards for Dalits, and a state-socialist economy. It culminated in a rationalist, socially engaged Navayana Buddhism that Ambedkar offered as an alternative to Hinduism and to Marxist violence.
scope: Based on Ambedkar's own writings and speeches (Annihilation of Caste 1936, States and Minorities, the 1949 Constituent Assembly speech, Buddha or Karl Marx) and the Ambedkarite Dalit-Buddhist movement as described in reference sources. Excludes party-political electoral strategies of later Dalit parties.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a focus of his writings; inferred from his state-socialist duty of the state to protect vulnerable groups.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from his labour-party record and view that the state must prevent exploitation by private employers.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He wrote that liberty from state control is another name for the dictatorship of the private employer and wanted the state to plan production.

public-ownership.rationale: His state socialism proposal made key industries, insurance and basic industries state-owned.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from his aim of just distribution; no specific tax rate is documented in the sources opened.

unions-good.rationale: He founded the Independent Labour Party and treated the working class as a central constituency against capitalism and Brahminism.

property-fundamental.rationale: His scheme subordinated private property in land and industry to state ownership and compensated owners in bonds.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He held that the state must plan economic life and prevent economic exploitation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from his demand for state protection of the poor and untouchables against exploitation.

worker-ownership.rationale: He favoured state rather than worker ownership; cooperative ownership is not a documented position.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; his stress on constitutional safeguards cuts one way and state-security concerns the other.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the Ambedkarite Buddhist ethic that includes abstaining from intoxicants.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred from his demand that Untouchables be made full citizens protected from caste abuse; no free-speech ruling documented.

strong-leader.rationale: He warned that hero worship and a leader beyond criticism endanger democracy.

state-harmful.rationale: He wanted a strong state to plan the economy and enforce rights; the stateless view is the opposite of his program.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his nonviolence-leaning Buddhism and rule of law.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his emphasis on constitutional morality over coercive power.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; he attacked devadasi-type exploitation but adherents differ on legal status.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the compassion-centred social ethics of Navayana.

traditional-family.rationale: He sought legal reform of Hindu family law (Hindu Code Bill) to give women divorce and property rights.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from his liberty-equality-fraternity principle and modern Ambedkarite stances.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from his support for birth control and women's autonomy.

more-religion-public.rationale: He saw religion as moral principle rather than public ritual and disliked caste religion's public role; not stated in these terms.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He backed reserved seats, jobs and education for Scheduled Castes; caste is the analogue, not race.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from his treatment of women's subordination as produced by Brahminical texts and custom.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He attacked inherited custom and scripture that sustained caste, so preservation of tradition for its own sake is rejected.

gradual-change.rationale: He demanded destruction of the caste system and rejection of shastra authority, though through constitutional means.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; he sought outside attention for untouchables but no documented view on the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from his state-led industrialisation emphasis; his monetary writings are not directly on trade.

nation-first.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; Buddhist ethics and rights-universalism pull in different directions.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened.

limit-growth.rationale: He promoted industrialisation to absorb surplus agricultural labour; inferred rejection of limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from his belief that state planning should steer the economy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from his industrialisation and Deweyan pragmatism; he held social reform to be the harder problem.

revolution-justified.rationale: He urged constitutional methods and warned against bloodshed and the grammar of anarchy.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from his insistence that political democracy rest on equal one-person-one-vote participation.

central-planning.rationale: His state socialism had the state plan economic life for the highest productivity, with private enterprise allowed to remain.

socialized-markets.rationale: He kept room for private enterprise alongside state ownership; worker-run markets are not his model.

land-value-tax.rationale: His land policy was state ownership and leasing, not a single land tax; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from his aim of just distribution; not documented.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from state duty to protect the vulnerable; not documented.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from his state-led industrialisation program.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He wrote that the state should supply capital for agriculture and industry and run key industries.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He criticised uneconomic small holdings and proposed state-owned land farmed collectively in standard sizes.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: His program kept wages and money; abolition is a communist aim he did not adopt.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: He wrote on currency and favoured a stable rupee, so abolishing central banking is far from his views.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from his preference for parliamentary democracy over state-recognised estates.

one-party-rule.rationale: He opposed permanent dictatorship and favoured parliamentary multiparty government.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rank contradicts his equality principle and opposition to birth-based status.

democracy-best.rationale: He held political democracy must be anchored in social democracy and defended parliamentary government over dictatorship.

direct-votes.rationale: He drafted a representative parliamentary constitution; referendums are not discussed.

workers-councils.rationale: He favoured parliamentary democracy and state ownership instead of councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: He accepted partition on specific communal grounds but defended the Union's unity in the Constitution.

natural-rulers.rationale: He denied that birth or varna fits anyone to rule and rejected graded inequality.

political-violence-never.rationale: He warned against bloodshed and preferred constitutional methods, though he allowed self-defence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from Buddhist ethics of non-violence.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Constitution he drafted is secular; he rejected religious law as a basis for state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He demanded that the shastras' authority be denied and burned the Manusmriti.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from his reliance on state enforcement of fundamental rights.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Buddhist-influenced rejection of militarism.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Inferred from his civic constitutional nationhood built on equal citizenship.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He saw class conflict but insisted caste is a division of labourers and that economic interpretation alone is inadequate.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He said political equality coexists with social and economic inequality that must end.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: He supported Scheduled Tribe protections; land authority is not explicit.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of religion-based political identity beyond rights.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred from Navayana social ethics grounded in fraternity and compassion.

duties-before-rights.rationale: His constitutional order stresses enforceable fundamental rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred from Buddhist ethics of compassion toward living beings.

limit-population.rationale: He supported birth control as part of economic development.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He championed industrialisation and urban escape from caste villages.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Pro-industry, but disruption of institutions is not discussed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from his stress on accountable human deliberation.

restore-past-order.rationale: He rejected Brahminical past order as the source of caste oppression.

results-over-ideology.rationale: His thought was shaped by Dewey's pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: He pursued constitutional and legal change, though he led the Mahad satyagraha.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred from his Buddhist ethic and insistence on constitutional morality.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred from his drive toward industrialisation and education.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: He attacked caste as a division of labourers, not division of labour itself.

distribute-by-need.rationale: He spoke of just distribution without specifying a need principle.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from state-planned production for productivity and fair distribution.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He named capitalism, with Brahminism, as an enemy of workers and said private property yields exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: In Buddha or Karl Marx he rejected permanent dictatorship and violence, favouring parliamentary rule.

collective-farming.rationale: He proposed state-owned land leased for collective cultivation by village residents.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He called capitalism an enemy of workers but made no documented claim about imperialist war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred from his reliance on state finance.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from his liberty principle; not explicitly stated.

individual-rights-only.rationale: He sought group safeguards such as separate electorates and reserved seats.

conscription.rationale: His sources do not address compulsory military service, and constitutional duties pull both ways.

exit-over-voice.rationale: He fought for citizenship-based voice though he did advise leaving Hinduism.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from his view that the state should protect welfare not run for profit.

positive-liberty.rationale: He said liberty without state limits on employers is dictatorship of the private employer.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not stated; he did criticise Brahmin dominance of public posts.

hereditarian-race.rationale: He rejected racial-origin explanations for caste hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Rejecting caste-based representation by birth; he wanted equal individual votes.

total-state.rationale: He valued fundamental rights and liberty as limits on the state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred from his preference for constitutional reform over decadence narratives.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: He opposed bound feudal-type relations such as the khoti and Mahar watan systems.

bound-labor.rationale: He legislated against khoti and attacked hereditary labour bonds.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: He argued Brahmins monopolised knowledge but also stood for reason and universals.

universal-morality.rationale: He grounded liberty, equality and fraternity as universal principles and Dhamma as moral law.

single-common-good.rationale: He regarded Indian society as composed of unequal interests needing safeguards.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in any source opened; no adherent consensus can be inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed in any source opened, so no position can be inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from his labour politics; his program favoured state control more than workplace votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from his demand for public education access for untouchables.

economic-freedom.rationale: He denied that liberty from state control serves the poor.

rule-by-example.rationale: He relied on constitutions and laws rather than ruler exemplars.

national-self-determination.rationale: He supported partition on communal grounds and separate representation.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Buddhist non-violence.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Navayana rejects karma, rebirth and the supernatural in favour of rational social ethics.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; his equal-citizenship focus gives no clear rule on immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from state duty to protect the vulnerable.

class-collaboration.rationale: He named capital and Brahminism as enemies of workers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; he valued libraries and education highly.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; he focused on caste not North-South geopolitics.

workers-nation.rationale: He framed workers by caste and class within India.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He pushed the Hindu Code Bill for equal rights and resigned when it was defeated.

ban-interest.rationale: He wrote on currency and credit; no prohibition is documented.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Compulsory graded segregation is what he fought as untouchability.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He saw the state as a tool that could be used for social justice, not only domination.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from his pluralist minority safeguards.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred; no support for conspiracy narratives.

proportional-representation.rationale: He weighed cumulative voting and other systems; no firm view in the sources opened.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred from Buddhist-universal rather than national-missionary ethic.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: He documented Brahminical scripture's subordination of women and legislated against it.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He said the state must plan economic life and prevent exploitation.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He treated intermarriage as the real remedy for caste; race is not his category.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He held equality as the only governing principle and demanded full citizenship for the Depressed Classes.

socialism-one-country.rationale: His state socialism was national in scope and he gave no view on world revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: He pressed reform of personal law for equal rights and supported a uniform code as a directive principle.

restrict-conversion.rationale: He himself left Hinduism and led mass conversion to Buddhism.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of Brahminical food taboos; sources opened do not detail it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from his secular constitutional stance.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of permanent dictatorship.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He grounded constitutional legitimacy in a people's constitution and universal adult suffrage.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; mercantilism inferred as unlikely.

population-transfer.rationale: In Thoughts on Pakistan he discussed exchange of populations, but this is contested among followers.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He accepted state coercion for law enforcement.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; liberty and safeguard concerns pull both ways.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: His critique treats caste as domination by graded privilege.

separated-powers.rationale: He designed an independent judiciary with fundamental-rights guarantees.

vanguard-party.rationale: He rejected communist dictatorship and favoured parliamentary democracy.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He wanted the state to protect vulnerable groups and equitable rights for the rural poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened; state land ownership model suggests no clear view.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He favoured birth control but attributed poverty mainly to social and economic structure.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred from his pluralist minority-rights approach.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from his elected representative constitution.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He emphasised protecting rights and constitutional morality.

party-controls-media.rationale: He valued liberty and parliamentary accountability over party control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Ambedkar never discussed party command of the army; rejection is inferred from his constitutionalism.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from his worry about hero worship and weak parliamentary independence.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not addressed; he wrote for a single Indian federation.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He designed a parliamentary system with a constitutional head of state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred from Navayana's lay, rationalist character.

clerical-rule.rationale: Ambedkar condemned Brahmin priestly authority and wanted the state free of religious rule, which clearly implies rejecting clerical government, though no source addresses that statement directly.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from his warning against concentrations of power.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed; he favoured fixed-term representative institutions.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from leased-land model.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: He called the village a sink of localism and urged escape to cities.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: He supported partition; no stated view.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Education was central to his program (educate, agitate, organise).

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He judged cultures by whether they uphold equality, rejecting caste culture.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from Buddhist ethics; he reportedly supported abolition.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from his birth control support.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; liberty and moral-ethics concerns pull both ways.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from his civic citizenship ideal.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: He attacked custom as a force suppressing individuals.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He framed the constitution through the Constituent Assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: He held political democracy essential and attacked dictatorship.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources opened.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He drafted indirect election of a parliamentary head of state.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from his acceptance of partition as a peace settlement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: His program subordinated property to social justice and state-ownership.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: He criticised Soviet-style dictatorship but gave no capitalism label.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He sought reform of religious institutions that sanction caste.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: His design had a constitutional head above the executive.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He called the Union indestructible, though accepted partition.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Reported to oppose special status for Kashmir; indirect.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Ambedkar attacked the scriptural sanction of graded hierarchy, which clearly implies rejecting a sacred head of state of divine descent, though he did not discuss it directly.

character-from-environment.rationale: His Deweyan pragmatism and caste analysis blame social environment.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He insisted on constitutional morality and rule of law.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources opened.

mixed-constitution.rationale: He rejected rule by hereditary or caste few.

leader-cult.rationale: He warned that hero worship can lead to dictatorship.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; his family-law work targeted women's equal rights in marriage.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state-socialist model.

land-redistribution.rationale: He proposed taking over land and leasing it to villagers, with compensation.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; he discussed population exchange at partition but not return.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: He openly left Hinduism and led mass conversion.

women-must-cover.rationale: He criticised purdah and subordination of women.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; his currency writings concerned the rupee standard.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: He pursued reserved representation more than cultural autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: He urged struggle within India and converted rather than emigrate.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He argued caste is not merely economic, favouring religion and ideas too.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He designed enforceable rights that majorities cannot override.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from his equal rights for women.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not stated; inferred from outward-looking modernism.

moral-incentives.rationale: Buddhist ethic favours moral motivation but no incentive doctrine documented.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He rejected bloodshed and revolution by force.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Abolishing birth-based privilege is the core of his anti-caste program.

history-own-civilization.rationale: He wanted history critically examined, including Brahminical record.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from equality principle; he opposed rule by a graded elite.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: He backed reserved seats for Scheduled Castes; race analogy inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: He held both that capitalism exploits and that state intervention can reform it.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; he treated Indian workers as divided by caste.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: He called liberty from state control the dictatorship of the private employer and fought exclusion.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He shaped fundamental rights enforceable in courts.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: He designed a representative republic with universal adult suffrage.

minority-veto.rationale: He sought minority safeguards, not vetoes; the principle is unworkable under his majority rule.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He supported constitutional methods of redress.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He favoured parliamentary government within the constitution.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Adherents differ; he did not oppose meat-eating.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He rejected trusteeship by privileged groups as feudal.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He led political organisation and held political power essential.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; he did say religion and custom reproduce hierarchy.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: He argued Brahminism wins the consent of every caste via graded privilege.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; his analysis was internal to India.

party-own-road.rationale: He charted a distinct path, rejecting Soviet-style doctrine.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He opposed dictatorship in both forms.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to slavery and caste.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; he burned the Manusmriti as symbol.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; his gender writing concerned women's subordination.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from his focus on women's subordination.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He defended liberal democracy as suited to India and rejected cultural-relativist defences of caste.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He insisted on civilian constitutional government.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from his women's economic rights stance.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; he criticised the hierarchical family but no filial doctrine is documented.

office-by-exam.rationale: He supported public service access but also reservations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from state control of key industries.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: He pursued divorce rights for Hindu women through the Hindu Code Bill.

land-use-tenure.rationale: He proposed state ownership of land leased to cultivators.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: His reservations logic treats unequal outcomes as evidence of structural exclusion.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from consent and rights principles.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from concern over private employer power.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his liberty and association principles.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from state duty to prevent exploitation.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, so no position can be inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: He stressed constitutional morality and rule of law.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He warned of hero worship and weak constitutional morality but defended parliamentary politics; no populist claim documented.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred from his non-violent ethic and constitutional politics; he did not adopt revolutionary defeatism.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He warned that political equality without social and economic equality would endanger democracy and judged Congress by whom freedom served.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from his parliamentary-government design and constitutional morality.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from his universalist rights and anti-oppression ethics, which do not rule out outside action against atrocities; he did not address the question directly.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from his Independent Labour Party record and state-socialist support for organised labour; he did not take a stand on industrial versus craft form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: His politics defended persecuted minorities and Dalits against majoritarian prejudice and rested on equal moral worth, so conspiracy claims against a minority contradict it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: He drafted the Hindu Code Bill to give women legal rights in marriage and property, which presumes legal marriage; inferred, not stated as a position on abolition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from his constitutional-democratic commitment to accountability and enforceable citizen rights; transparency law was not an issue he addressed.

local-production.rationale: He saw the Indian village as a cesspool of caste and favoured state-planned industrialisation over village self-sufficiency; inferred from that critique.

informal-organisation.rationale: He built formal parties, unions and organisations (Independent Labour Party, Scheduled Castes Federation) and relied on constitutional methods.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He stressed the constitution's supremacy but never addressed international courts; adherents are not clearly aligned.

religious-nation.rationale: He rejected a Hindu-defined nation and defended a secular constitutional community of equal citizens, while his Buddhist conversion was a personal and social choice, not a national definition.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from his commitment to equality and rejection of hierarchy, including in foreign relations; the topic is not in his writings.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: He favoured a strong unified constitutional state with state-owned key industries and agriculture, so retention of revenue by regions is inferred as disfavoured.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: His state socialism puts industry and agriculture under state ownership but leaves personal property alone; this is inferred from the proposals in States and Minorities.

defeat-communism.rationale: He rejected violent communism but argued from democratic means and did not campaign to defeat communist states; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: His state-socialist plan has the state own and run key industries and insurance, so private providers are inferred as disfavoured.

religion-illusion.rationale: Ambedkar held that religion is a necessary moral basis for society, which is why he promoted Navayana Buddhism rather than treating religion as an illusion.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: He pursued women's rights through law and the Hindu Code Bill rather than through economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Domestic labour is outside his stated programme; adherents are split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not in his writings; inferred from his liberal-constitutionalist and rationalist outlook that he opposed such purges.

treaties-binding.rationale: He argued for entrenched constitutional safeguards for minorities that the majority cannot amend unilaterally; this is extended to treaties by inference.

cooperative-communities.rationale: He rejected Gandhian village republics as caste-bound and favoured a modern constitutional state; communal self-rule is inferred as disfavoured.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from his equal-citizenship principle and his protection of minorities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Navayana Buddhism is offered as an alternative to Hinduism and to Marxist violence, and state socialism within democracy as a middle course; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from his insistence on equal individual rights over claims grounded in birth or descent.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his rationalist, rights-based politics.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from his commitment to liberty and equality under a constitution.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He defended constitutional parliamentary democracy and enforceable rights, warning against abandoning constitutional methods.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He rejected the shastras and religious sanction for social order and offered a rationalist Navayana Buddhism instead.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from his equality principle and his opposition to domination of one group by another.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his rejection of religious violence and his rationalist outlook.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from his insistence on constitutional methods and his rejection of violent change.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He called democracy a form of associated living and fellow-feeling, and stressed ordinary people's participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: He treated caste and class as intertwined, saying caste is a division of labourers, and he backed group safeguards.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his equality principle and rights-based constitutionalism.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; no documented position and adherents' views vary.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred from his own position: he was a social reformer on the left and was not trying to combine both camps.

alienated-labor.rationale: In Buddha or Karl Marx he shares Marx's concern with exploitation but not his methods; inferred from his state-socialist economics.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from his critique of religious orthodoxies and his support for minority protections.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He grounded authority in the people through the Constitution and rejected scriptural sanction.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; his secular state does not map clearly onto dress rules and adherents differ.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his support for enforceable rights and protections for the weak.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not addressed directly; he proposed state ownership of key industries, so he would reject a mixed model of this kind.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his role in framing a state with armed forces under civilian control, and the Buddhist ideal is not absolute pacifism.

rich-first.rationale: The rich-first formula is never addressed; rejection is inferred from his commitment to economic equality.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; no documented position on blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Ambedkar's 1949 speech rejects hero-worship and defends equality and a republic, which are incompatible with inherited office.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from his state-socialist proposals under which key industries and insurance are state-run rather than left to profit-making or mutual lenders.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed by Ambedkar; his state-socialist economics might favour sovereignty but the sources do not say.

property-franchise.rationale: Ambedkar's 1949 speech defends one person, one vote, one value as the basis of political equality.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not a theme in his writings.

reification.rationale: Ambedkar rejected Marxist class analysis as the main frame and argued caste was the primary structure; no direct statement on reification.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: His 1949 speech warns that political democracy cannot last without social and economic democracy, so formal freedoms are hollow under steep inequality.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: He insisted on constitutional morality and rule by law over personal rule, and rejected the shastras as arbitrary authority.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement rests on equality and the abolition of birth-based hierarchy, so it opposes racial or caste-based exclusion from government.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed; he lived before the internet.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from his insistence on accountable constitutional government.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Annihilation of Caste urges intermarriage as a means to dissolve caste, so restricting marriage across communities runs against his view.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from his equality principle and opposition to caste-based social boycott, which Dalits suffered.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Ambedkar's 1949 speech defends constitutional parliamentary democracy with representatives and enforceable rights; sortition is not discussed, so this is inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He rejected the authority of the shastras and urged judging doctrine by reason and social ethics, and Navayana recasts Buddhism rationalistically.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Ambedkar held that economic power and caste privilege defeat liberty and equality, and wanted key industries and agriculture under the state.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from his equal-citizenship principle and liberty-equality-fraternity; he never addressed the question.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: he promoted a rationalist Buddhism by conversion, not state-run atheist education, and wanted a secular constitutional state.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from his commitment to constitutional order and rule of law as the route to social democracy.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He demanded group safeguards such as separate electorates and reserved seats for Dalits rather than plain majority rule.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: His state-socialist program made the state, not private charity, responsible for the poor and the outcaste.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed in his writings; adherents are not divided by it and his concern was representation of Dalits, not office tenure.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: he defended representative parliamentary democracy with enforceable rights rather than direct delegation.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: A modern question he never addressed and nothing in his principles settles it.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from his insistence on equality and his Navayana Buddhism, which opened its social ethics to women.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: He drafted the Hindu Code Bill to give women equal rights in marriage, divorce and property.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Ambedkar's equal-citizenship principle is compatible with it, but local voting for foreigners is not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from his state-socialist view that the state must prevent exploitation by private owners.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not discussed in his writings.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not addressed in the sources used; adherents' views are not documented.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from Navayana's ethic of non-violence and compassion.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; his concern is internal caste oppression.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: His state-socialist programme put key industries and agriculture under state or collective ownership so that income would not flow from landlordism or capital.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Navayana stresses non-violence, but Ambedkar did not make an absolute pacifism central, and this is not documented in the sources.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: He rejected the Brahminical-Hindu national myth and its sanction of caste, so an unbroken ancient national continuity is inferred to be doubted.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; his concern is caste rather than sex and gender theory.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, though he backed legal equality for women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed; no martyr cult features in the sources.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Navayana frames religion as social ethics, but the good-versus-evil spiritual framing of politics is not stated.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora and homeland questions are not addressed.

culture-before-state.rationale: He insisted political democracy needs social democracy via constitutional safeguards, so state-building and rights come together rather than culture first.

god-not-male.rationale: Navayana Buddhism is non-theistic, so God language is largely not at issue.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: He judged Hindu scriptures by their treatment of the oppressed including women, and championed the Hindu Code Bill for women's rights.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: He fought for minority safeguards and reserved seats for Dalits, against dominance by the majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed in the sources used.

independent-unions.rationale: Ambedkar led the Independent Labour Party and defended labour's rights against employers; independence from the state is inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Ambedkar's state socialism was coupled with parliamentary democracy and a rejection of Marxist dictatorship, so social ownership without democratic power would not count; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: He proposed state ownership of key industries and public provision, which covers essential services.

second-chamber.rationale: He helped draft a Constitution with a Council of States alongside the House of the People; his own view of bicameralism is inferred from that.

municipal-property.rationale: His programme vests key industries and agriculture in the state, not in local communities, and he distrusted village localism.

confederal-coordination.rationale: He favoured a strong Union over village autonomy, which he called a den of localism and caste; inferred rejection of confederal localism.

family-wage.rationale: Wages are not addressed in the sources; no stated view on family-based pay.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug-approval speed is not discussed in the sources, so neutral is the honest answer.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ageing research is not discussed in the sources, so neutral is the honest answer.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Payment privacy is not discussed in the sources, so neutral is the honest answer.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity is not discussed in the sources, so neutral is the honest answer.

person-over-state.rationale: Liberty, equality and fraternity and the dignity of each individual against caste are central to his case; he stressed the individual as the unit of worth.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Navayana Buddhism offered a moral and spiritual basis for social life beyond material goods, as Ambedkar's alternative to Marxism.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: He favoured a strong centre and powers allocated by the Constitution; inferred agreement that the national legislature is final authority.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetically engineered crops are not discussed in the sources, so neutral is the honest answer.

dense-cities.rationale: He called the Indian village a sink of localism and urged Dalits to leave it for cities; inferred preference for cities.

racial-group-interests.rationale: He opposed organising politics by caste-group Hindu identity but sought group safeguards for Dalits; on race as such, inferred rejection.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed for race; he stressed dignity and self-respect of Dalits rather than pride in birth.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Navayana Buddhism's ethic of non-violence is inferred to favour force only in defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Ambedkar saw the Indian nation as a political community built on equal citizenship and warned that caste and religious division stopped it being one; he did not ground nationhood in language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for the Depressed Classes and accepted reserved seats under the Poona Pact, but he did not seek religious electorates as such and later favoured joint electorates; adherents read this differently.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: he treated caste and internal social division as India's main weakness and wrote on Pakistan as a political demand, not as a foreign plot.

free-public-college.rationale: He founded colleges for the depressed classes and pressed for state support for their education; free tuition is inferred from his state-socialist economics.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not a concern of his writings and anachronistic.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; his emphasis was on ending present social hierarchy.

women-distinct-values.rationale: He championed women's equality (Hindu Code Bill) but did not claim women bring distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from Navayana Buddhism's non-violence, which he offered as an alternative to violent revolution; he also backed a strong army for India.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from his state-socialist programme of state ownership of key industries and insurance, which implies state economic control; he wrote nothing on capital movements.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Ambedkar's constitutional democracy rests on rule of law and state-enforced rights, from which a state monopoly on force is inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Ambedkar encouraged Dalit military service and accepted defensive war, though the Buddhist side leans toward non-violence; refusal as a rule is unlikely.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party and backed trade unions and labour protection.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from his state-socialist support for state provision for the poor; the specific mechanism is not discussed.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Ambedkar wrote on public finance and sound currency but also wanted heavy state investment; no stated view on borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: His economic writing focused on India and caste, not international economic rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: He chose constitutional parliamentary democracy and rejected violent revolution, offering Buddhism as the alternative to Marxist violence.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: States and Minorities lays out a fixed state-socialist economic blueprint rather than leaving economies open.

sacred-nation.rationale: He wanted national fraternity but stressed that caste prevents a nation, and he rejected sacralised religious claims on society.

student-debt-relief.rationale: He prized education for Dalits and favoured state support; debt relief is inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed in these terms; he analysed caste rather than regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: He grounded rights in the equal dignity of the individual under liberty, equality and fraternity, though his Buddhism is rationalist and ties morality to social conduct.

public-service-media.rationale: He ran his own newspapers because the mainstream press excluded Dalits, but he never set out a view on public broadcasting.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Ambedkar judged religions by their social morality and rejected Hinduism while adopting Buddhism, treating religions as rival rather than equivalent.

farm-price-support.rationale: His States and Minorities plan put agriculture under state ownership and collective farming, protecting cultivators from landlords and moneylenders.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Ambedkar did not address nuclear arms; Navayana non-violence and support for national defence pull in opposite directions.

workers-own-party.rationale: He founded the Independent Labour Party in 1936 and later the Scheduled Castes Federation to give labouring and Dalit people their own political vehicle.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from his insistence on equality and enforceable rights against custom sanctioned by the shastras.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: He championed equal inheritance and property rights for women through the Hindu Code Bill and held custom sanctioned by religion could not override equality.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed in the sources used; Ambedkar favoured a national official language but the question of regional names is not covered.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from his state-socialist economics, which favour public regulation over private-law remedies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary chiefs are not an Indian institution he discussed; rejection is inferred from his opposition to hereditary and caste authority.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from his priority on constitutional rights and equality; environment was not a theme of his work.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from his commitment to constitutional due process and equal treatment; sentencing policy was not addressed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; he backed a common national language but nothing on immigrant requirements.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from his labour organising and state-socialist view that workers need strong collective bodies; he did not address dues rules.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from his insistence on universal adult franchise and on removing barriers to the vote for the excluded.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from his secular constitutional order, which gave no religion legal precedence; he did not discuss sects within a religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: His 1949 speech says political democracy is hollow without social and economic democracy, so elections alone do not suffice.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from his demand for equality of women and his Hindu Code Bill; he did not discuss premarital sex directly.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from his stress on enforceable constitutional liberties; he never addressed the internet.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from his state-socialist preference for state provision over a single cash transfer; anachronistic.

women-suffrage.rationale: He championed universal adult franchise and equal political rights, which the 1949 speech frames as one person, one vote.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: He argued the shastras subordinate women and drafted the Hindu Code Bill to give them rights, though his target was Brahmanical Hinduism rather than all religion.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of Aryan-race theories and treatment of caste as a social, not natural, division.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from his drive for women's legal equality through the state; he did not discuss such agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from his state-socialist proposals in States and Minorities, which put land and key industries under state ownership rather than first-come private claims.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from his constitutionalism and rule-of-law stance; he did not address international courts directly.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: He urged denying the authority of the shastras and, as Navayana Buddhism, treated religious texts as open to reason rather than infallible.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from his commitment to equality and the Constitution's guarantees of equal rights; he did not discuss Indigenous self-government in these terms.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from his state-socialist economics, though he criticised authoritarian rule and rejected Marxist violence, so support is qualified.

indirect-election.rationale: He defended parliamentary democracy with direct popular voting as the instrument of political democracy in his concluding speech.

national-church-status.rationale: He rejected Hindu religious hierarchy and favoured a state with equal rights, treating state privilege for Hindu religion as incompatible with equality.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Adherents are split: he sought group safeguards for Dalits but was wary of ethnic autonomy that would entrench communal divisions; inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred as indifferent.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from his support for a unified Indian state under a constitution, though he did not discuss colonial borders as such.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: he held that the village was a sink of localism and advocated modern, urban and industrial life over self-sufficient village living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; he backed protections for Scheduled Tribes but did not discuss limits on settlement.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from his principle of equal rights and treatment regardless of birth, extended to gender; conscription is not discussed directly.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Ambedkar rejected Hindu cultural nationalism and its sacralised homeland; this is inferred from that rejection, as he never addressed land and nation in these terms.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: His Constituent Assembly speech insists on constitutional methods and rule of law, which leaves no room for killing suspects without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Ambedkar never addressed relations with China as a great power; he opposed Marxist violence but no stance on alignment can be inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: His safeguards concern minorities inside India; support for kin abroad is not addressed and is not inferable.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: His States and Minorities proposals put agriculture and key industries under state ownership, so benefit from land and resources goes to society.

self-ownership.rationale: His stress on liberty and dignity implies personal rights over body and labour, though state socialism qualifies it; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax structure on consumption is not addressed in the sources; adherents have no settled view.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He fought for targeted safeguards for Dalits and Scheduled Castes; inferred that adherents favour need-based targeting, though universal provision is also compatible with state socialism.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: He defended parliamentary democracy and warned against hero worship and bypassing institutions, treating parties and an opposition as necessary.

no-business-privileges.rationale: State socialism puts economic power under public rules rather than favoured private firms; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: He demanded equal citizenship regardless of religion and opposed Hindu-dominated politics; inferred, as his own safeguards were for castes, not denominations.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Navayana Buddhism is rationalist and breaks with Hindu tradition, so he would not make a return to ancestral values the aim; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: As law minister he drafted the Hindu Code Bill, which sought to give Hindu women rights including divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: State socialism places land and key industries under state ownership, which implies national rather than foreign control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from his state-socialist proposals for state ownership and collective agriculture, which treat the resulting pattern of holdings as a matter for the state.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed in his writings; no stated view on taxing financial transactions.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Racism is not his subject; by analogy, he held that caste discrimination remained the chief obstacle for Dalits, so he would reject the claim.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: He burned the Manusmriti and denied the shastras authority, but in 1949 he rejected unconstitutional methods once constitutional ones existed; inferred as a mild rejection.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from his support for industrialisation, labour protections and state planning; he did not discuss automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed; his concern was caste and the Indian constitution, not the structure of world power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: He disputed Marxism's account of history and violence, but the labour theory of value itself is not discussed in the sources.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: In the 1949 speech he asked whether Indians would put country above creed and urged fraternity, while his programme centred on workers and the oppressed.

material-over-identity.rationale: He argued that socialists must first abolish caste, since caste divides workers; Dalit recognition is central to him, not secondary to class interests.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: He rejected the Marxist dictatorship of the proletariat and violent one-party rule in favour of parliamentary democracy.

missingStatements.text: Caste or birth-based hierarchy should be abolished and not merely reformed.
missingStatements.rationale: Ambedkar held nothing can emancipate the outcaste except destruction of the caste system and urged denying the shastras' authority.

missingStatements.text: Members of historically excluded groups should have reserved seats, jobs and education places.
missingStatements.rationale: He backed reservations for Scheduled Castes and Tribes and fought for reserved seats at the Poona Pact.

missingStatements.text: Inter-caste marriage and shared dining are the real way to break down hierarchy.
missingStatements.rationale: Annihilation of Caste treats breaking the barriers to fusion of castes as the remedy; Roy's introduction presents this as central.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to caste in one tradition; abolish-hereditary-privilege and equal-moral-worth cover its ideological content.

notes: Ambedkar's Annihilation of Caste text itself was only reached via Roy's introduction in the archive.org copy; several statement answers are inferences from his general principles and are marked low. Strands: Navayana Buddhists, secular Dalit-Bahujan activists and Ambedkarite Marxists differ on religion and economics.
